correctness.rationale: The normalized series has b_0=b_1=1, b_2=epsilon_s and b_(n+1)/b_n<=q^(kappa_s n), so truncation after x² costs O(q^(3 kappa_s)) with all fixed derivative orders on compact x disks. The positive-zero Hadamard product for B and the product for D=B+u x B' justify the radial extremum: finite products give strictly positive D roots via the derivative of x^(1/u) B(x) and Rolle interlacing; local uniform convergence/Hurwitz preserves the positive-root location, and the coefficient bound gives order zero for D. A first pole occurs for D before B (the real logarithmic derivative of B forces D/B through zero), including when a=1 and the B term in C drops out. With weights u, m(a-1), m all nonnegative, each logarithmic-derivative sum has its disk bound at positive real x. For |w-1|<delta, the logarithm power series gives |log w|<=-log(1-|w-1|)<1. The first e^(-1) roots therefore give the exact radii, not just lower bounds. Setting B=1-x and D=1-vx gives the stated X_star and the quadratic for X_c (its value at 1/v is -um/v); the roots are simple and below the poles. For a factor 1-beta x+gamma epsilon x², the perturbation of its logarithmic derivative is gamma(2x-beta x²)/(1-beta x)². Applying this to (beta,gamma)=(1,1) and (v,1+2u) gives exactly both Y's by the negative reciprocal slopes, with a positive leading displacement and O(epsilon_s²) residual. The mth root, exact lambda ratio and epsilon_2=q epsilon_3 yield the stated radius ratio. This covers the coincident f and g at nu=1 and uses no uniformity as nu goes to zero. The finite high-precision support checks were read as evidence, not executed or used to certify the universal claim.

value.rationale: The result quantifies a natural exact geometric threshold in a singular parameter limit. It explains why the two base families have the same scaled first data yet different genuinely sharp correction orders, and gives the first coefficient of their radius comparison for each normalization and both geometric properties. The correction and its sign are not obtained from the leading scaling or from a numerical approximation to the implicit equations. No novelty or value is assigned to re-stating those equations.
